evidence.quote: Most Dwarf words have several meanings.
evidence.claim: Select the stated glossary sense; these two- and three-word compositions are adaptations, not attested complete item names or a complete grammar.

evidence.quote: Dok Watch, observe, see, the eye
evidence.claim: Dok supplies an eye motif, not a claim of a seeing or intelligent artifact; bryn and duraz are the selected shining and stone motifs from this page.
Grong and grungron supply craft motifs, while grim uses the unyielding sense; these names do not assert item type or mechanical durability.
Karaz, karak, kol and skarrenruf supply mountain, enduring, black and bright-blue motifs; no new vocabulary is inferred.
Ungor, zan, zharr and zon supply cavern, red, fire and sun motifs. Fire in a name does not grant fire effects.

evidence.section: Thorgrim Grudgebearer / Magic Items / The Axe of Grimnir
evidence.claim: Named ancestral artifacts are particular identities with provenance. The Axe of Grimnir is reserved, and none of its history or powers is assigned.
The Hammer of Angrund, its Ironhammer alias and Shield of Defiance are reserved identities, not reusable artifact labels.

evidence.section: Rune Weapons of Renown, Loremaster source anchor offset 224384
evidence.quote: it is the runesmith who names the weapon
evidence.claim: This older official source directly attests naming prized rune weapons by their maker, and then explains that an owner may name an unnamed one. Using symbolic titles for mundane DF artifacts is an explicit gameplay adaptation; it does not manufacture a runesmith or make an item magical.
Exclude the otherwise composable Zandok because it collides with a named canonical character surname.
Dok Karaz is an established fortress and gatehouse identity. Exclude its normalized name from native template products; Karazdok is a separately reviewed compact symbolic proposal.

evidence.claim: The OCR-spaced name denotes an established Dwarf hold lost to Daemons. Reserve Dok Duraz in normalized form; native template generation must not reuse it as a new artifact identity. The compact proposal Durazdok is separately evaluated.

Drakk supplies only the dragon motif. Applying colour or shine to this symbolic title is a new composition; it does not certify a slaying, trophy, bound creature, dragon-made object, power, or actual engraved design.

evidence.section: Khazalid Glossary: Gorl, Grund, Gronti, Gor
evidence.claim: The selected senses are yellow, hammer, giant and wild beast. Gorl does not assign gold material, Grund does not classify the item as a hammer, and creature imagery does not invent a species, deed or animal-derived material.
The chisel is an ordinary craft-object motif. Neither the object named nor its maker needs to be a chisel or a sculptor; no engraving or crafting event is generated.
The Black Hammer brewing clan is a canonical identity. Its compact name is reserved here as well as globally, rather than used for a generated artifact.
Az supplies the war-axe image; Azul selects metal of any kind and Baraz selects a promise. Exact-type/material affinity needs separate item evidence. A promise title does not create an oath.
